steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the bow tie pasta and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, about 12 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic, olive oil, and cabbage; season with salt and pepper; cook until tender, about 15 minutes. Stir in the sausage and bow tie pasta; cook until completely heated, about 5 minutes more. Top with Parmesan cheese and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Cabbage and Smoked Sausage Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Try this simple and quick pasta dish for a tasty, low-effort dinner.

review.reviewBody:
This is a great recipe for cabbage lovers -like me. My prep is alittle different. I use the same ingredients but slice rather than shred and I also throw in a big sliced onion and about a cup of beef stock. Into the big frying pan it all goes until tender. Finally I dump the pasta in a well I made in the middle of the cabbage and align pieces of the sausage around the pan like spokes on a wagon wheel for presentation. (I fry the sausage first - sometimes I use Keeebassa)

Good recipe. I made a few changes based on recs from others, plus a few of my own. I browned the kielbasa in 2 T butter and removed from pan. I added 2 Tbsp olive oil to pan and sauted 1/2 a small cabbage, sliced, 1 sliced onion, 1 sliced red pepper and added 1/2 tsp caraway seeds. I covered & cooked about 15 min., stirring occasionally. Then I added the sausage and 8 oz. of penne pasta. I sprinkled 2 cups o cheddar over the top and mixed in and served.

My husband and I both enjoyed this dish. I think the next time I make it, I will add a 1/2 pkt of dry Italian dressing mix. Thank you for the recipe!
Update:
I made it again and this time:
In a skillet slice up sausage in bite size pieces. Melt 2T of butter and add cabbage, garlic, shredded carrots and a stalk of celery chopped into bite size pieces. Cook until the vegetables are crisp tender. If you like your sausage browned, cook it a bit before adding vegetables.

When the pasta is cooked and drain, add 1-2T butter, 3-4T Italian salad dressing (this replaces the olive oil). Add the skillet content and stir to distribute oils, add the parmesan and stir until well coated. Enjoy :)

I make this all the time, it's a family favorite. I do not use smoked sausage, I use bacon and omit the oil and butter. I chop the bacon and cook till crisp and remove from the pan and drain on paper towel, I saute an onion along with the cabbage right in the bacon fat, and I use extra wide egg noodles. In my house we call this dish lazy mans pierogies.

Made it using 1/2 large onion, 3 cloves garlic, 1/2 head small cabbage, 2 links smoked chicken sausage - saute in non-stick skillet with 1 tsp. evoo and 1 tsp. butter. Had 1/2 C left-over extra wide noodles chopped up. More than enough for 2, a lot fewer calories, and very, very tasty.

A new regular dinner for rotation. I did as others and added onion and halved oil and butter. Much much better the next day. A lot more flavor. In the future I will make everything but the noodles, the night before. Then make noodles fresh and mix in, after reheating meat and veggies.

I made this the other day just because it reminded me of a recipe I used to make when I was first married a thousand years ago, I learned the recipe from my grandmother. I make my own pasta which gives it a rougher surface that absorbs the butter and oil rather than having it on the bottom of the dish. I also bought a homemade sausage from a local sausage maker here in Maine, but most importantly (I think is this dish requires that you cut the cabbage a certain way), don't just buy a bag of shredded cabbage, cut fresh in roughly in thick slices. I used about a teaspoon of fennel seed and skipped the parmesan cheese altogether. It was very much like my grandmother used to make.

Very sorry, but one half cup of butter is ridiculous. Look at those calorie and fat gram numbers and know that you can make this with 1-2 teaspoons of butter, or no butter at all, just olive oil. Also, I use a thinly sliced onion in it, with 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon of minced garlic after the onions are sauteed to transparency. The pasta, in my opinion, is superfluous as all it does is add what most of us do not need, which is more carbs. When I make this dish I add just a touch of chicken base with a splash of water, perhaps a half teaspoon, then adjust the salt only at the end. You have enough fat calories in the sausage, which is great to have now and then. Just my take on what is a comforting dish on any night of the week.

This is a great way to use cabbage. Only cook the cabbage for about 5 min. I cooked the sausage first, used skinless smoked sausage, wiped the pan out so did not have to much oil. Used less butter and oil based on previous reviews. used more garlic, and a little more parmesan. It is an easy and yummy recipe!! Will make it again.

We browned the sausage, then removed from the pan and cooked the cabbage in the drippings and olive oil, until it started to brown before adding the garlic and cooking for a couple minutes. Mixed in the cooked sausage, 1T butter and pasta, then topped with the parmesan just before serving. Made this way, we loved it.
The recipe as written seems like it would be terribly greasy.
I followed recipe and I used 5 minute steamable Brussel sprouts instead of cabbage, then I added precooked shrimp and 1 sliced onion. So good!!
The base recipe is a little bland. However, simplicity has its own value. I followed the base recipe, although my cabbage was a tad small.

I didnt have bow tie pasta so I substituted with tricolor rotini pasta, also had green onions that needed to be used so I chopped them up and sautéed with the cabbage. Hubbie says he loved it, so I say it’s a keeper!
Add caraway seeds, red pepper flakes, sliced onion, and a little bit of milk at the end. Delish!

I thought this turned out great! I added one chopped onion, more garlic and used medium shell pasta…didn’t need the olive oil at all even though I used less than the butter called for. I also added 1 tsp seasoning salt, a few shakes of pepper and a little bit of cilantro for color. I’ve made a version of this meal many times but never thought to add Parmesan cheese before…it works!
Easy to make added carrots and onions.

I added some spices to our liking: onion & garlic powder, smoked paprika, more salt and pepper. I cut back on the butter because of other reviewers comments. I wish I'd cut way back on the pasta, because it was too much, I used about 8 oz. And the next time, I won't cook the cabbage for 15 min., it was too much. I may make this one again.
My whole family loves this recipe!! And it’s not hard to make either!!! Highly recommend!!
Perfect as written! I have been making this for 30 years, only I use hot Italian sausage and lots more parm. Sometimes I use cauliflower instead of cabbage, and that is equally good.
Was really good! Will need to scale it back, it's a lot for two lol
